newsitem.title: USA: Kodak holders OK proposal for board election.
newsitem.headline: Kodak holders OK proposal for board election.

text.p: Shareholders of Eastman Kodak Co Wednesday approved a measure urging the board of directors to change by-laws so directors are elected annually.
George Fisher, chairman and chief executive officer, announced the results at the company's annual meeting in Greeley, near Kodak's second largest U.S. manufacturing site in Windsor, Colo.
With 80 percent of all outstanding shares voting, 50.3 percent of shares voted in favor of the proposal, and 49.7 percent voted against it.
Fisher said the proposal urges the 11-member board "to take the necessary steps" to switch from the current staggered board voting.
Fisher said that while corporate by-laws do not require the board to adopt the measure, "our board will seriously consider the recommendation."
If the board put a measure to switch to annual elections before holders next year, 80 percent of votes would have to approve the change.

Dan Carp, president and chief operating officer, also said that the company has no plans to cut product prices. "Slashing prices doesn't work in the long run," Carp said during a presentation to holders.

Fisher said the company continues to hold to its long-term objective of "at least 10 percent" annual earnings per share growth. Fisher also said he expects Kodak "to outperform the industry average growth rate."
In answer to a shareholder question, Fisher said the company has no plans to move from its current headquarters in Rochester, N.Y. to Greeley. The question drew laughter from the audience.
Fisher said about 3,000 Kodak employees and retirees live in Colorado, along with about 2,000 shareholders.
Fisher declined to answer a question on how the company's businesses were faring during the current quarter.
